questions.q: $The solution curve of the differential equation, \left(1 + e^{- x}\right)  \left(1 + y^{2}\$right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$y^{2}$~which passes through the point \left(0, 1\right)$, is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\left(1 + e^{- x}\right)\left(1 + y^{2}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y^{2}$

Separate variables

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + y^{2}\right)dy}{y2} = \dfrac{dx}{1 + e^{- x}}$

Integrate both side

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{\left(1 + y^{2}\right)dy}{y2} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{1 + e^{- x}}$

$⇒ ∫ \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{y2}\right)dy = ∫ \dfrac{e^{x}dx}{e^{x} + 1}$

$⇒ y - \dfrac{1}{y} = ln \left(e^{x} + 1\right) + C$

Since curve pass through~\left(0, 1\right)$.

$⇒ 1 - $\dfrac{1}{1} =$ln \left(e^{0} + 1\right) + C ⇒ C = - ln \left(2\right)$

$⇒ y - $\dfrac{1}{y} =$ln \left($e^{x} + 1\right) - ln \left($2\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{y^{2} - 1}{y} =$ln $\$left(\dfrac{e^{x} + 1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ y^{2} = 1 + y\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{1 + e^{x}}{2}\right)$

$

questions.q: If the solution curve of the differential equation \left(  \left(\tan^{- 1}$y\right) - x\right)dy = \left($1 + y^{2}\right)dx$~passes through the point \left($1, 0\right)$ then the abscissa of the point on the curve whose ordinate is $tan  \left(1\right)$ \text{ and } is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left(\tan^{- 1}y - x\right)dy = \left(1 + y^{2}\right)dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} + \left(\dfrac{1}{1 + y^{2}}\right)x = \dfrac{\tan^{- 1}y}{1 + y^{2}}$

I.F.~$= e^{∫ \dfrac{1}{1 + y^{2}}dy} = e^{\tan^{- 1}y}$

General solution will be

$x\left(e^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) = ∫ e^{\tan^{- 1}y} \times \dfrac{\tan^{- 1}y}{1 + y^{2}}dy$

$⇒ x\left(e^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) = \tan^{- 1}y\left(e^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) - e^{\tan^{- 1}y} + C$

Since the curve~passes through \left(1, 0\right)⇒ C = 2$

So, the curve reduces to $x\left(e^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) = \tan^{- 1}y\left(e^{\tan^{- 1}y}\right) - e^{\tan^{- 1}y} + 2$

when~$y = tan1, x\left(e\right) = 1\left(e\right) - e + 2$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2}{e}$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + xe^{y - x}, - \sqrt{2} < x < \sqrt{2}, y  \left($0\right) = 0$,~then~the minimum value of y\left($x\right), x \in \left(- $\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}\right)is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + xe^{y - x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy - dx}{ey - x} = xdx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(y - x\right)}{ey - x} = ∫ xdx$

$⇒ - e^{x - y} = \dfrac{x2}{2} + c$

At $x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ c = - 1$

So, the particular solution is~

$e^{x - y} = \dfrac{2 - x^{2}}{2}$

$⇒ y = x - ln \left(\dfrac{2 - x^{2}}{2}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$1 + $\dfrac{2x}{2 - x^{2}} = \dfrac{2 + 2x - x^{2}}{2 - x^{2}}

$⇒ $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^{2} - 2x - 2}{x^{2} - 2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^{2} - 2x - 2}{\left(x + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(x - \sqrt{2}\right)}

If~\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$0 ⇒ x^{2} - 2x - 2 = 0$

$⇒ x = $\dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{12}}{2}

$⇒ x = 1 $\pm \sqrt{3}

So minimum value occurs at $x = 1 - $\sqrt{3}

$y \left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right) = \left($1 - $\sqrt{3}\right) -$ln \left(\dfrac{2 - ( 4 - 2\sqrt{3} )}{2}\right)

$= \left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right) - ln \left(\sqrt{3} -1\right)$

$

questions.q: Let& $y = y  \left(x\right)$~ be the solution curve of the differential equation \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x}  \left(1 + x^{2} \left($1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)\right)$, $x > 0, y ( 1 ) = 3$. Then $\dfrac{y^{2} ( x )}{9}$is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given differential equation can be rewritten as,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{x} = y^{3} \left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)$

\dfrac{1}{y3}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{xy2} =$1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x$

Let~\left(- $\dfrac{1}{y2}\right) =$t ⇒ $\dfrac{2}{y3}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}

$∴ $\dfrac{dt}{2dx} + \dfrac{t}{x} = \left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dt}{dx} + \dfrac{2t}{x} =$2\left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right) . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

We know the solution of the differential equation~\dfrac{dy}{dx} +$Py = Q$~is given by,

${ye}^{∫ Pdx} = ∫ {Qe}^{∫ Pdx} + C ( WhereI . F . = e^{∫ Pdx} )$

Therefore, on solving equation(1)~we get,

I.F.$= e^{∫ $\dfrac{2}{x}$dx} = x^{2}$

\dfrac{- x^{2}}{y2} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\left($1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)x^{3} - $\dfrac{x3}{3}\right) +$C . . . . . . ( 2 )$

Given,$y ( 1 ) = 3$

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{9} = -$2\$left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{9}\right) +$C$

$∴ C = $\dfrac{5}{9}

Now putting value of C in equation(2) we get,

\dfrac{y2}{9} = \dfrac{x2}{5 - 2x^{3}\left(2 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x^{3}\right)}

$

questions.q: Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation, \dfrac{dy}{dx} +$ytanx = 2x + x^{2}tanx, x \in \left(- $\dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{π}{2}\right),~such that $y\left(0\right) = 1 .& Then$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + ytanx = 2x + x^{2}tanx$

This is a linear differential equation of the type~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$~where~$P = tanx \text{ and } Q = 2x + x^{2}tanx$

Now,~the integrating factor~$I . F . = e^{∫ Pdx} = e^{∫ tanxdx}$

$= e^{lnsecx} = secx$

And, the general solution is~$y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

$y ⋅ secx = ∫ \left(2x + x^{2}tanx\right)secxdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2xsecxdx + ∫ x^{2}\left(secx ⋅ tanx\right)dx + c$

Using integration by parts in the second integral, we get

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2xsecxdx + x^{2} ∫ \left(secx ⋅ tanx\right)dx - ∫ \left(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{2}\right) ∫ \left(secx ⋅ tanx\right)\right)dx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = ∫ 2xsecxdx + x^{2} ∫ secxdx - ∫ 2xsecxdx + c$

$⇒ ysecx = x^{2}secx + c$

$⇒ y = x^{2} + c \cdot cosx$

Now,~$y\left(0\right) = 1$

$⇒ 0 + c = 1 ⇒ c = 1$

So,~$y = x^{2} + cosx$

Hence,~$y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$~and~$y\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Differentiating~$y ( x )$~with respect to~$x$

$⇒ y^{'}\left(x\right) = 2x - sinx$

Hence,~$y^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{π}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}$~and~$y^{'}\left(- \dfrac{π}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{π}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ y^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) - y^{'}\left(- \dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \pi - \sqrt{2} .$

questions.q: The slope of the tangent to a curve $C: y = y  \left(x\right)$ at any point $[ x, y )$ on it is \dfrac{2e^{2x} - 6e^{- x} + 9}{2 + 9e^{- 2x}}.If $C$ passes through the points  \left(0, $\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{π}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)and \left(\alpha, $\dfrac{1}{2}$e^{2\alpha}\right)$ then $e^{α}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2e^{2x} - 6e^{- x} + 9}{2 + 9e^{- 2x}}$

On rearranging we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{2x} - \dfrac{6e^{x}}{2e^{2x} + 9}$

Integrating both side we get,

$y = \dfrac{e2x}{2} - \sqrt{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}e^{x}}{3}\right) + c$

If the curve~passes through the point \left(0, \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{π}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)$

Then~$c = \sqrt{2} \left(\dfrac{π}{4} + \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{2}{3}\right)

So, curve will be~$y = $\dfrac{e2x}{2} - \sqrt{2}\left(\tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}e^{x}}{3}\right) - \dfrac{π}{4} - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{2}{3}\right)

Again curve~passes through the point

\left(\alpha, \ddfrac{1}{2}e^{2\alpha}\right)$~

Putting the value in curve equation we get,

$\dfrac{e2\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{e2\alpha}{2} - \sqrt{2} \left(\tan^{- 1}\$left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}e^{α}}{3}\right) - \dfrac{π}{4} - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{2}{3}\right)

$⇒ \tan^{- $1}\$left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}$e^{α}}${3}\right) = \dfrac{π}{4} + \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\sqrt{2}e^{α}}{3} =tan $\$left(\dfrac{π}{4} + \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{2}{3}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}e^{α}}{3} = \left(\dfrac{tan\dfrac{π}{4} + {tantan}^{- 1}\dfrac{2}{3}}{1 - tan\dfrac{π}{4} \times {tantan}^{- 1}\dfrac{2}{3}}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}e^{α}}{3} =\$left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{2}{3}}{1 - \dfrac{2}{3}}\right)

$⇒ e^{α} = $\dfrac{3}{2} $\$left(\dfrac{3 + \sqrt{2}}{3 - \sqrt{2}}\right)

questions.q: $Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$ be a solution of the differential equation, \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \sqrt{1 - y^{2}} =$0, \left|x\right| < 1 .$~If $y  \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2},then y\$left(\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{1 - y^{2}} + \dfrac{dx}{1 - x^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}y + \sin^{- 1}x = c$
At,$x = \dfrac{1}{2}, y = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} ⇒ c = \dfrac{\pi}{2} ⇒ \sin^{- 1}y = \cos^{- 1}x$
Hence,~$y\left(\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = sin\left(\cos^{- 1}\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: Let $x=x(y)$ be the solution of the differential equation $y^2 \mathrm{~d} x+ \lleft(x-\frac{1}{y}\right) \mathrm{d}y=0$. If $x(1)=1$, then x\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& y^2 d x+\left(x-\frac{1}{y}\right) d y=0 \\
& y^2 d x=\left(\frac{1}{y}-x\right) d y \\
& \Rightarrow y^2 \frac{d x}{d y}=\frac{1}{y}-x \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{d y}+\frac{x}{y^2}=\frac{1}{y^3} \\
& \text { I.F. }=e^{\int \frac{1}{y^2} d y}=e^{\frac{-1}{y}}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Solution is
$x e^{\frac{-1}{y}}=\int e^{-\frac{1}{y}} \times \frac{1}{y^3} d y+C$
Let $\frac{-1}{y}=t\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{y^2} d y=d t \\
& \Rightarrow x e^{-\frac{1}{y}}=-\int e^t t d t+C \\
& \Rightarrow x e^{-\frac{1}{y}}=-e^t(t-1)+C \\
& \Rightarrow x e^{-\frac{1}{y}}=-e^{\frac{-1}{y}}\left(\frac{-1}{y}-1\right)+C
\end{aligned}x(1)=1\Rightarrow e^{-1}=-e^{-1}(-2)+C\Rightarrow C=-e^{-1}\Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{y}+1-e^{-1+\frac{1}{y}}x\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=3-e$

questions.q: If $y = y ( x )$ is the solution curve of the differential equation \left(x^{2} - 4\right)dy - \left(y^{2} - 3y\right)dx = 0$, $x > 2, y ( 4 ) = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and the slope of the curve is never zero, then the value of $y ( 10 )$ equals :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

\left(x^{2} - 4\right)dy - \left(y^{2} - 3y\right)dx = 0$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y^{2} - 3y} = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x^{2} - 4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ \dfrac{y - ( y - 3 )}{y ( y - 3 )}dy = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x^{2} - 4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ \left(\dfrac{1}{y - 3} - \dfrac{1}{y}\right)dy = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x^{2} - {2}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3}\left(log | y - 3 | - log | y |\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}log\left|\dfrac{x - 2}{x + 2}\right| + C$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3}log\left|\dfrac{y - 3}{y}\right| = \dfrac{1}{4}log\left|\dfrac{x - 2}{x + 2}\right| + C$

At $x = 4, y = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3}log\left|\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{2} - 3}{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right| = \dfrac{1}{4}log\left|\dfrac{4 - 2}{4 + 2}\right| + C$

$⇒ 0 = \dfrac{1}{4}log\left|\dfrac{1}{3}\right| + C$

$⇒ 0 = - log \left|3\right|$\dfrac{1}{4} +$C$

$⇒ C = $\d$dfrac{1}{4}log\left($3\right)$

$⇒ $\ddfrac{1}{3}log\left|$\dfrac{y - 3}{y}\right| = \ddfrac{1}{4}$log\left|$\dfrac{x - 2}{x + 2}\right| + \dfrac{1}{4}log ( 3 )$

Putting, $x = 10$

$⇒ $\ddfrac{1}{3}log\left|$\dfrac{y - 3}{y}\right| = \ddfrac{1}{4}$log\left|$\dfrac{2}{3}\right| + \dfrac{1}{4}log ( 3 )$

$⇒ $\ddfrac{1}{3}log\left|$\dfrac{y - 3}{y}\right| = \ddfrac{1}{4}$log\left|$2\right|$

$⇒ $log\left|$\dfrac{y - 3}{y}\right| = \dfrac{3}{4}log2$

$⇒ log \left|$\dfrac{y - 3}{y}\right| =log \left(2\dfrac{3}{4}\right)$

$⇒ - y + 3 = 8\dfrac{1}{4} \cdoty$

$⇒ 3 = \$left(8\dfrac{1}{4} +$1\right)y$

$⇒ $\dfrac{3}{1 + \left(8\right)\dfrac{1}{4}} =$y$

questions.q: Let $y = y  \left(t\right)$ be a solution of the differential equation~\dfrac{dy}{dt} + \alphay = \gammae^{- \betat}~Where, $\alpha> 0, \beta> 0$~and $\gamma> 0$. Then ${Lim}_{t \to \infty}y  \left(t\right)$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} + \alphay = \gamma \cdot e^{- \betat}$

Which is a linear differential equation,

So, integrating factor will be~$I . F = e^{∫ \alphadt} = e^{\alphat}$

So, the solution of differential equation is given by

$y \times e^{\alphat} = \gamma ∫ e^{- \betat} \times e^{\alphat}$

$⇒ y \times e^{\alphat} = \gamma ∫ e^{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)t}$

$⇒ y \times e^{\alphat} = \gammae^{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)t}\left(\alpha - \beta\right) + c$

$⇒ y = \gammae^{- \betat}\left(\alpha - \beta\right) + ce^{- \alphat}$

Now finding~$\lim_{t \to \infty}y$~we get,

$\lim_{t \to \infty}y = \lim_{t \to \infty} \left(\gammae^{- \betat} \left(\alpha - \beta\right) +$ce^{- \alphat}\right)$

$⇒ \lim_{t \to $\infty}y = $\gamma \times$0 + c \times0 = $0\left$\{\text{as}$e^{- $\infty} \to 0\right\}

$

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{{2}^{x - y}  \left({2}^{y} -1\right)}{{2}^{x} - 1} = 0, x, y > 0, y\left(1\right) = 1$, then $y\left(2\right)& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{{2}^{x - y}\left({2}^{y} - 1\right)}{{2}^{x} - 1} = 0x, y > 0, y\left(1\right) = 1$

Now rearranging and integrating both side of $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{{2}^{x}\left({2}^{y} - 1\right)}{{2}^{y}\left({2}^{x} - 1\right)}$,~we get

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{2y}{{2}^{y} - 1}dy = - ∫ \dfrac{2x}{{2}^{x} - 1}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{ln2} ∫ \dfrac{{2}^{y}ln2}{{2}^{y} - 1}dy = - \dfrac{1}{ln2} ∫ \dfrac{{2}^{x}ln2}{{2}^{x} - 1}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{ln2}ln\left|{2}^{y} - 1\right| = \dfrac{- 1}{ln2}ln\left|{2}^{x} - 1\right| + C$

At~$x = 1, y = 1$

Putting this values in above equation~we get~$C = 0$

So,~$ln\left|{2}^{y} - 1\right| + ln\left|{2}^{x} - 1\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left({2}^{x} - 1\right)\left({2}^{y} - 1\right) = 1$

$⇒ {2}^{y} - 1 = \dfrac{1}{{2}^{x} + 1}$

At~$x = 2$

$⇒ {2}^{y} = \dfrac{1}{3} + 1 = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$y = \log_{2}\dfrac{4}{3} = \log_{2}4 - \log_{2}3 = 2 - \log_{2}3$

questions.q: If a curve $y=y(x)$ passes through the point  \left(1, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and satisfies the differential equation \left(7 x^4 \cot y-e^x \operatorname{cosec} y\right) \frac{d x}{d y}=x^5, x \geq 1$, then at $x=2, the value of cosy is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{7 \cot y}{x}-\frac{e^x \operatorname{cosec} y}{x^5} \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{7 \cot y}{\sin y \cdot x}-\frac{e^x}{\sin y x^5} \\ & \sin y \frac{d y}{d x}-\cos y \cdot \frac{7}{x}=\frac{-e^x}{x^5} \\ & \text { let }-\cos y=t \\ & \sin y \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d t}{d x}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d t}{d x}+\frac{7 t}{x}=\frac{-e^x}{x^5} \\ & \text { I.F. }=x^7 \\ & \text { t. } x^7=-\int x^2 e^x d x \\ & \operatorname{cosy} x^7=x^2 e^x-2 \int x e^x d x \\ & \operatorname{cosy} x^7=x^2 e^x-2 x e^x+2 e^x+c \\ & x=1, y=\frac{\pi}{2}, c=-e \\ & \operatorname{cosy}=\frac{2 e^2-e}{128} \\ & \text { option }(3)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let& $y = y  \left(x\right)$~be solution of the differential equation~$\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) =3x + 4y,$~with~$y\left(0\right) = 0$.~If~$y\left(- \dfrac{2}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2\right) = \alpha\log_{\mathrm{e}}2$,~then the value of~$\alpha& is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

$\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = 3x + 4y$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{3x} \cdot e^{4y}$

$⇒ ∫ e^{- 4y}dy = ∫ e^{3x}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{e- 4y}{- 4} = \dfrac{e3x}{3} + C$

Given,

$y\left(0\right) = 0$

So,

$- \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{3} = C ⇒ C = - \dfrac{7}{12}$

So, the particular solution is

$\dfrac{e- 4y}{- 4} = \dfrac{e3x}{3} - \dfrac{7}{12}$

$⇒ e^{- 4y} = \dfrac{4e^{3x} - 7}{- 3}$

$⇒ e^{4y} = \dfrac{3}{7 - 4e^{3x}} ⇒ 4y = ln \left(\dfrac{3}{7 - 4e^{3x}}\right)$

$4y = ℓn \$left(\dfrac{3}{6}\right)$~when~$x = - \dfrac{2}{3}ℓn2$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{4}ℓn \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$⇒ y = - \dfrac{1}{4}ℓn2$

So,~$\alpha = - \dfrac{1}{4}$

questions.q: If $x = x  \left(y\right)$~is the solution of the differential equation y\dfrac{dx}{dy} =$2x + y^{3} \left(y + 1\right)e^{y}, x  \left(1\right) = 0$; then $x\left(e\right)$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{2x}{y} = y^{2}\left(y + 1\right)e^{y}$~ ~

Finding integrating factor~$I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{- 2}{y}dx} = e^{- 2lny} = \dfrac{1}{y2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{y2} = ∫ \left(y + 1\right)e^{y}dy$~ ~

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{y2} = y \cdot e^{y} + C$

$0 = e + C ⇒ C = - e$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{y2} = ye^{y} - e$

Putting~$y = e$~in the equation we get

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{e2} = e . e^{e} - e$

$⇒ x = e^{3} \left(e^{e} - 1\right)&

$

questions.q: Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation, x\dfrac{dy}{dx} +$y = x\log_{\mathrm{e}}x,  \left(x > 1\right)$. If $2y  \left(2\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}4 - 1$, then $y\left(e\right) is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given differential equation& can be written as

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = \log_{\mathrm{e}}x$, which is a linear differential equation.

Now, integrating factor $I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = e^{lnx} = x$

Hence, the solution of the given differential equation~is

$y \cdot x = ∫ x \cdot \log_{\mathrm{e}}xdx$

$⇒ y \cdot x = \log_{\mathrm{e}}x ∫ xdx - ∫ \left\{\dfrac{1}{x} ∫ xdx\right\}dx$~(using integration by parts)

$⇒ y \cdot x = \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\left(\dfrac{x2}{2}\right) - ∫ \dfrac{1}{x} \cdot \dfrac{x2}{2}dx$

$⇒ y \cdot x = \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\left(\dfrac{x2}{2}\right) - ∫ \dfrac{x}{2}dx$

$⇒ xy \left(x\right) = $\dfrac{x2}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}$x - $\dfrac{x2}{4} +$C . . . \left(1\right)$

Putting~$x = 2$~we get,~

$⇒ 2y\left(2\right) = 2\log_{\mathrm{e}}2 - 1 + C$

$⇒ 2y\left(2\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}4 - 1 + C$

Given,~$2y \left(2\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}4 - 1$

Then we get,~$C = 0$~

Now, from the equation~\left(1\right)$~we get,~

$y\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}x - \dfrac{x}{4}$

Putting~$x = e$~in above equation, we get,

$y\left(e\right) = \dfrac{e}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}e - \dfrac{e}{4} = \dfrac{e}{2} - \dfrac{e}{4} = \dfrac{e}{4}$

$

questions.q:
Let $y = y \left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation \dfrac{dy}{dx} ==$2x\left($x + y\right)3 - $x \left(x + y\right) - 1, y \left(0\right) = 1$. Then, $\$left(\dfrac{1}{2} ++$y\$left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)2$ equals:

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x\left(x + y\right)3 - x\left(x + y\right) - 1$

Let, $x + y = t$

$⇒ 1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx} - 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} - 1 = 2xt^{3} - xt - 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} = 2xt^{3} - xt$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} + xt = 2xt^{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{t3}\dfrac{dt}{dx} + \dfrac{x}{t2} = 2x . . . \left(i\right)$

Putting, \dfrac{1}{t2} =$u$

$⇒ $\dfrac{- 2}{t3}\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{t3}\dfrac{dt}{dx} = \dfrac{- 1}{2}\dfrac{du}{dx}

Putting this value in equation \left(i\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{- 1}{2}\dfrac{du}{dx} +$xu = 2x$

$⇒ $\dfrac{du}{dx} -$2xu = - 4x$

Integrating factor, $IF = e^{∫ - 2xdx}$

$⇒ IF = e^{- x^{2}}$

So, solution of the given differential equation is,

$u \timese^{- x^{2}} = ∫ e^{- x^{2}}\left(-4x\right)dx$

$⇒ $\dfrac{e- x^{2}}{t2} =$∫ e^{- x^{2}}\left(-4x\right)dx$

Putting, $- x^{2} = z$

$⇒ - 2xdx = dz$

$⇒ $\dfrac{e- x^{2}}{\left(x + y\right)2} =$∫ 2e^{z}dz$

$⇒ $\dfrac{e- x^{2}}{\left(x + y\right)2} =$2e^{z} + C$

$⇒ $\dfrac{e- x^{2}}{\left(x + y\right)2} =$2e^{- x^{2}} + C$

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{\left(x + y\right)2} =$2 + Ce^{x2}$

It is given that, at $x = 0$, $y = 1$.

$⇒ 1 = 2 + C$

$⇒ C = - 1$

$⇒ \left(x + y\right)2 = $\dfrac{1}{2 - e^{x2}}

Putting, $x = $\dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ \left(y + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{2 - e^{\dfrac{1}{2}}}$

$⇒ \left(y \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$2 = $\$left(\dfrac{1}{2 - \sqrt{e}}\right)$

$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation $x\log_{\mathrm{e}}x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = x^{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}x, ( x > 1 )$. If $y ( 2 ) = 2$, then $y ( e )$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

$xlnx\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = x^{2}lnx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{xlnx} = x$

This is a linear differential equation.

Now, finding integrating factor we get

$I . F = e^{∫ \dfrac{1}{xlnx}dx} = e^{ln\left(lnx\right)} = lnx$

Now, solution of the differential equation is given by

$y \times I . F = ∫ \left(x \times I . F\right)dx$

$⇒ y \times lnx = ∫ xlnxdx$

$⇒ y \times lnx = lnx \cdot \dfrac{x2}{2} - \dfrac{x2}{4} + c$

Now given~$y\left(2\right) = 2$,

$2 \times ln2 = ln2 \cdot \dfrac{22}{2} - \dfrac{22}{4} + c$

$⇒ c = 1$

So, equation will be~$y \times lnx = lnx \cdot \dfrac{x2}{2} - \dfrac{x2}{4} + 1$

Now finding~$y \left(e\right)$~we get,

$y \timeslne = lne \cdot $\dfrac{e2}{2} - \dfrac{e2}{4} +$1$

$⇒ y \times1 = 1 \cdot $\dfrac{e2}{2} - \dfrac{e2}{4} +$1$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{4 + e^{2}}{4}$

$

questions.q: Suppose& $y = y  \left(x\right)$~be the solution curve to the differential equation~\dfrac{dy}{dx} -$y = 2 - e^{- x}$~such that~$\lim_{x \to \infty}y  \left(x\right)$~is finite. If~$a$~and~$b$~are respectively the~$x -$~and~$y -$intercept of the tangent to the curve at~$x = 0$, then the value of~$a - 4b$& is equal to _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = 2 - e^{- x}$

Linear differential equation,

So,~$I . F . = e^{- ∫ dx} = e^{- x}$

Now~solution of differential equation is given by~

$y \times IF = ∫ \left(2 - e^{- x}\right) \times IFdx$

$⇒ ye^{- x} = ∫ \left(2 - e^{- x}\right)e^{- x}dx$

$⇒ ye^{- x} = ∫ \left(2e^{- x} - e^{- 2x}\right)dx$

$⇒ ye^{- x} = - 2e^{- x} + \dfrac{e- 2x}{2} + C$

$⇒ y = - 2 + \dfrac{e- x}{2} + Ce^{x}$

Given~$\lim_{x \to \infty}y$~is finite

So,~$\lim_{x \to \infty}\left(- 2 + \dfrac{e- x}{2} + C \cdot e^{x}\right) \to$finite

This is possible only when~$C = 0$

Hence$y = y\left(x\right) = - 2 + \dfrac{e- x}{2}$

Now finding the slope~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \dfrac{1}{2}e^{- x}$

${\dfrac{dy}{dx}}_{x = 0} = - \dfrac{1}{2} = m, y\left(0\right) = - 2 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{- 3}{2}$

Now~equation of tangent will be,

$y + \dfrac{3}{2} = - \dfrac{1}{2} \left(x - 0\right)$

$⇒ x + 2y = - 3$

x-intercept~$a = - 3,$~y-intercept~$b = $\dfrac{- 3}{2}

So,~$a - 4b = - 3 + 6 = 3

$

questions.q: If the curve, $y = y  \left(x\right)$ represented by the solution of the differential equation \left(2xy^{2} - y\right)dx + xdy = 0$, passes through the intersection of the lines, $2x - 3y = 1$ and $3x + 2y = 8$, then $| y\left(1\right) |$ is equal to ___ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
\left(2xy^{2} - y\right)dx + xdy = 0$

$2xy^{2}dx - ydx + xdy = 0$

$2xdx = \dfrac{ydx - xdy}{y2} = d \left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)

Now integrate

$x^{2} = $\dfrac{x}{y} +$c$

Now point of intersection of lines are \left(2, 1\right)$.

$4 = $\dfrac{2}{1} +$c ⇒ c = 2$

$x^{2} = $\dfrac{x}{y} +$2$

Now $y\left(1\right) = - 1$

$⇒ | y\left(1\right) | = 1$

$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}+2 y \sec ^2 x=2 \sec ^2 x+3 \tan x \cdot \sec ^2 x$ such that $\mathrm{y}(0)=\frac{5}{4}$. Then $12 \left(\mathrm{y}  \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-\mathrme^{-2}\right)is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \text { I.F. } & =\mathrme^{\int 2 \sec ^2 x d x} \\ & =\mathrme^{2 \tan x}\end{aligned}$
Solution of diff. eq.
$\begin{gathered}y \cdot e^{2 \tan x}=\int e^{2 \tan x}\left(2 \sec ^2 x+3 \tan x \cdot \sec ^2 x\right) d x \\ y \cdot e^{2 \tan x}=\int e^{2 \tan x} \cdot\left(2 \sec ^2 x\right) d x+\int e^{2 \tan x} \cdot\left(3 \tan x \cdot \sec ^2 x\right) d x\end{gathered}$
y. $\mathrme^{2 \tan x}=\mathrme^{2 \tan x} \cdot 2 \tan x-\int \mathrme^{2 \tan x} \cdot 2 \sec ^2 x \times 2 \tan x d x+\int \mathrme^{2 \tan x} \cdot 3 \tan x \cdot \sec ^2 x d x$
$\begin{aligned} & y \cdot e^{2 \tan x}=2 \tan x \cdot e^{2 \tan x}-\int \mathrme^{2 \tan x} \cdot \tan x \sec ^2 x d x \\ & y . e^{2 \tan x}=2 \tan x \cdot e^{2 \tan x}-\frac{\tan x \cdot e^{2 \tan x}}{2}+\frac{e^{2 \tan x}}{4}+C\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & y=2 \tan x-\frac{\tan x}{2}+\frac{1}{4}+\mathrm{Ce}^{-2 \tan x} \\ & x=0, y=\frac{5}{4} \\ & c=1\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{y}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{7}{4}+\mathrme^{-2}$
Then $12\left(y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-\mathrme^{-2}\right)=12\left(\frac{7}{4}\right)=21$

questions.q: $Let a curve $y = y  \left(x\right)$ be given by the solution of the differential equation~cos  \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{- 1}\left($e^{- x}\right)\right)dx = \left(\sqrt{e^{2x} - 1}\right)$dy$.~If it intersects $y$-axis at $y = - 1$,~and the intersection point of the curve with $x -$axis is  \left(\alpha,0\right)$,~then $e^{α}$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$cos\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{- 1} \left(e^{- x}\right)\right)dx = \left(\sqrt{e^{2x} - 1}\right)$dy . . . \left($i\right)$

Put $\cos^{- 1} \left(e^{- x}\right) = \theta, \theta \in \left[0, \pi\right]$

$⇒ cos\theta =e^{- x}$

$⇒ 2\cos^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2} -1 = e^{- x}$

$⇒ cos\$left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{e^{- x} + 1}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{e^{x} + 1}{2e^{x}}}

Hence, by~ \left(i\right)$, we have

$cos \left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)dx = \$left(\sqrt{e^{2x} - 1}\right)$dy$

$⇒ $\sqrt{\dfrac{e^{x} + 1}{2e^{x}}}$dx = $\sqrt{e^{2x} - 1}$dy$

$⇒ \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{e^{x} + 1}{2e^{x}}}\right)$dx = \left(\sqrt{e^{x} - 1}\right) \left(\sqrt{e^{x} + 1}\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}∫ \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{e^{x}}\sqrt{e^{x} - 1}} =∫ dy$

Put $e^{x} = t ⇒ dt = e^{x}dx$

$\dfrac{1}{2}∫ \dfrac{dt}{e^{x}\sqrt{e^{x}}\sqrt{e^{x} - 1}} =∫ dy$

$∫ \dfrac{dt}{t\sqrt{t^{2} - t}} = \sqrt{2}∫ dy$

Put~$t = \dfrac{1}{z}⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dz} = - \dfrac{1}{z2}$

$∫ \dfrac{- \dfrac{dz}{z2}}{\dfrac{1}{z}\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{z2} - \dfrac{1}{z}}} = \sqrt{2}∫ dy$

$⇒ - ∫ \dfrac{dz}{1 - z} = \sqrt{2}∫ dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 2 ( 1 - z{)}^{1 / 2}}{- 1} = \sqrt{2}y + c$

$⇒ $2 \left($1 - $\dfrac{1}{t}\right)$1 / 2 = $\sqrt{2}$y + c$

$⇒ 2 \left($1 - e^{- x}\right)1 / 2 = $\sqrt{2}$y + c$

Now, it meets~$y - $\text{axis}~at~\left($0, - 1\right)$, hence

$0 = - $\sqrt{2} +$c ⇒ c = $\sqrt{2}

Hence,

$2 \left($1 - e^{- x}\right)1 / 2 = $\sqrt{2}\left(y + 1\right)$

It~passes through~ \left(\alpha, 0\right)$

$2\left(1 - e^{- \alpha}\right)1 / 2 = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{1 - e^{- \alpha}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 1 - e^{- \alpha} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ e^{- \alpha} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ e^{α} = 2$
